question.prompt:
The Math Team designed a logo shaped like a multiplication symbol, shown below on a grid of \(1\)-inch squares. What is the area of the logo in square inches?

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q01_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The grid lets us find the area by counting whole squares and half-squares. Inside the logo there are \(4\) complete unit squares and \(12\) right triangles, each formed by cutting a unit square along its diagonal.

Each square has area \(1\) square inch, and each triangle has area \(\frac12\) square inch. Therefore the logo has area

\[
4+12\cdot\frac12=10
\]

square inches. The answer is \(\boxed{10}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\). Pairing two half-squares is a useful way to count a slanted shape on a square grid.
solutions.title: Count complete grid squares and half-squares
